attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post. The Markoff quote is separate and is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: A compound present-state observation: AI comprehension is lacking and very few, if any, jobs have been replaced. The normalisation keeps the 'very few if any' quantifier and the 2022 endpoint.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: actual positions replaced, a small share, no country restriction. Comprehension means general, robust understanding. No threshold is invented. The result still depends on how 'very few' and 'comprehension' are read.

evidence.note: NBER study of US vacancies 2010–2018: reduced non-AI hiring at exposed establishments and no detectable aggregate employment effect. It covers a different period and scope and does not count gross jobs replaced worldwide through October 2022.
BIG-bench (June 2022) shows prompt brittleness on causal tasks for selected models. Relevant to robustness, but it is a narrow test, not a broad finding on general comprehension at the endpoint.

reviews.rationale: Both items lean toward Marcus but do not meet the support condition. e1 is US-only, ends in 2018 and measures hiring and aggregate employment, not gross displacement. e2 covers selected tasks only. Nothing in the packet shows substantial replacement or robust comprehension either. The packet's own gaps note that no representative displacement estimate was found.

attribution.note: Marcus's own evaluative sentence about the Caucheteux et al. study and the lead author's 'direct links' tweet.

semantics.note: 'Way too much charity' is evaluative, but underneath it is a testable claim that the study's evidence does not warrant a direct link. The normalisation captures that claim and ties it to GPT-2 and this study.

contract.note: Reading 'direct link' as a shared internal mechanism follows Marcus's own phrase 'functioning in the same way in both'. That is a fair, ordinary reading. Reading it as any statistical association would make the claim false by construction, so the interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: The author's dated thread describes the findings as a linear mapping of representations, a correlation with comprehension scores, and layer and attention effects. These are associations, and nothing in the thread distinguishes a shared mechanism from other explanations. The author calls them 'direct links' but offers no evidence of mechanism.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's reading, the author's own description shows only predictive mappings and correlations. Nothing in the packet establishes a shared internal mechanism. Her use of 'direct links' is a label, not evidence that would meet the contradiction condition. This meets the support condition, though the case rests on a single secondary reproduction of the thread.

attribution.note: Marcus's own tweet, which he quotes and endorses in his post. The replies from other people are not part of the claim.

semantics.note: The 'in some cases' qualifier is restored. The claim has two parts: radiologists' duties, and the relative suitability of convnets for those duties. It is an observation, not a forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'less suited' as a practical disadvantage, not total incapacity, is fair to the speaker. The 2022 reporting window is the evaluator's choice and pushes the 2021 professional source into context, but this does not change the result.

evidence.note: 2022 JACR review: radiology reports are mostly unstructured text and costly to review by hand. This partly supports the text-handling side of the work. It makes no architecture comparison.

2022 preprint: reports contain patient history in free text that computers find hard to interpret, and a transformer beat CNN baselines on extraction. This is weak support for 'less suited'. It does not compare text tasks with image tasks.
2021 professional paper: radiologists access patient histories and prior reports through hospital systems. Relevant to the duties component, but it predates the window.
2019 study: CNNs classified clinical text well in two of three tasks. This qualifies a broad reading of 'less suited', but it covers narrow classification, not reasoning over patient histories.

reviews.rationale: The duties component gets partial support: reports are unstructured and contain patient history. The core comparison, that convnets suit images better than history reasoning and free-text understanding, is not established. e2 compares architectures on text only, and e4 cuts the other way for narrow text tasks. The packet admits no study settles it, so the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own statistical point in his post.

semantics.note: A factual and mathematical claim about the study's R = 0.5 and its 'half unexplained' statement. The paper states 'half' outright rather than implying it, which makes no material difference.

contract.note: Treating the figure as the coefficient of determination for the bivariate correlation is the standard reading. The criteria are clear and fair.

evidence.note: The paper reports a correlation with comprehension of 'up to R = 0.50' and in the same passage says half of the comprehension variability remains unexplained. 0.5 squared is 0.25, so 75% remains unexplained.
Textbook statement that r² is the share of variability explained, obtained by squaring r. A mathematical identity, revised in 2023, before the evaluation date.

reviews.rationale: The study reports R = 0.50 and says half the comprehension variability is unexplained. Under the standard identity, R = 0.5 explains 25% of variance and leaves 75% unexplained. Marcus's correction holds. The reported private exchange with King was not verified and is not needed.
